Makes a window and shows it. Windows are the parents of every other gadget: pass the window as the group of a button, label or list to put it inside. The position is relative to the group, which is [Desktop](Desktop) for a normal window or another window to make a child that belongs to it.

The style is a sum of these flags, and 15 is the default:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Title bar |
| 2 | The user can resize the window |
| 4 | Menu bar, shown with a line under it even before menus are added, see [WindowMenu](WindowMenu) |
| 8 | Status bar at the bottom, see [SetStatusText](SetStatusText) |
| 16 | Tool window with a smaller title bar and only a close box |
| 32 | Width and height are the size of the inside, not of the whole window |

Windows send events when they move ($801), change size ($802), are closed ($803) or are activated ($804). Closing does not remove a window by itself, your program decides what to do with the $803 event.

```blitzbasic
;media interact windows/createwindow.gif 1
;media wait 400
;media click 265 34
;media wait 400
;media shot
Graphics 320, 240, 32, 2
win = CreateWindow("My window", 20, 20, 260, 180, Desktop(), 15)
CreateLabel "Try the X.", 20, 20, 200, 40, win
SetStatusText win, "Waiting"
asked = 0
Repeat
	e = WaitEvent()
	If e = $803 And EventSource() = win Then
		asked = asked + 1
		SetStatusText win, "Close was asked " + asked + "x"
	EndIf
Until asked = 2
```

![CreateWindow](media/windows/createwindow.gif)
@param title   Text in the title bar.
@param x       Horizontal position inside the group.
@param y       Vertical position inside the group.
@param width   Width of the window.
@param height  Height of the window.
@param group   Desktop or another window. Defaults to 0, which means the desktop.
@param style   Sum of the flags above. Defaults to 15.
@returns A handle for the window.
@difference Every window on the desktop is a window of the operating system, with its frame and title bar, so flag 1 only says whether the window has them, and the user moves, sizes, minimizes and maximizes it the way the system does. Menu bars and status bars are drawn by the runtime. Where no window can be made (no display, or `BLITZLLVM_HEADLESS`) the windows are drawn inside the window of `Graphics` instead, in the order they were activated. A program that uses the GUI still gets the window of `Graphics` (1024 by 768 where it did not ask for one); that window is where the mouse and key commands of BlitzBasic look, and closing it posts `$803` with source 0 instead of ending the program.
